title: Netsh PortProxy addition command
description: Detects a Netsh command requesting an interface PortProxy forwarding-rule addition, including explicit -c context syntax. Verify the resulting configuration and traffic before concluding that a proxy was established.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may add a Windows PortProxy rule to relay TCP connections through a compromised endpoint.
hypothesis.rationale: Netsh interface PortProxy add configures TCP forwarding. The ordered context, operation and translation family distinguish addition requests from unrelated strings; approved WSL and administration workflows may use identical syntax.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify the ordered PortProxy context, add operation and supported translation family, including -c context syntax; exclude show, deletion and unrelated firewall-rule text.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Validate the listener, destination and owner before escalation; WSL, connected-cache, development and administrative workflows can intentionally create PortProxy rules.
steps: Baseline this signal with the responsible application or endpoint owner; legitimate use is expected, and this event alone is not a compromise verdict.
Confirm the command's result in follow-on process, file, registry or service telemetry; a process-start event records intent and does not prove successful execution.
Review the complete Netsh command, listen and connect addresses and ports, original filename, parent process, account and endpoint role.
Inspect the active PortProxy configuration and correlate listening sockets, firewall changes, inbound connections and the destination service.
Confirm an approved WSL, cache, development or administration requirement; otherwise remove the forwarding rule safely, contain the endpoint and investigate related network activity.
false_positives: Approved WSL publishing, Microsoft Connected Cache, development testing or administrative TCP forwarding configured through Windows PortProxy

validation.expected_outcome: Match ordered PortProxy add syntax with standard translation families, tabs and -c contexts; reject unrelated marker text, queries and deletion.

limitations: Authorized administration can produce this event. The rule does not independently establish compromise or completion of a command; assess identity, target and change approval.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
